glosses: To receive, especially with a consent, with favour, or with approval.

examples.text: Remember all thy offerings, and accept thy burnt sacrifice.

glosses: To admit to a place or a group.

examples.text: The Boy Scouts were going to accept him as a member.

glosses: To regard as proper, usual, true, or to believe in.

examples.text: I accept the notion that Christ lived.

glosses: To receive as adequate or satisfactory.

examples.text: I accept your proposal, amendment, or excuse.

glosses: To endure patiently.

examples.text: I accept my punishment.

glosses: To acknowledge patiently without opposition or resistance.

glosses: To agree to pay.

glosses: To let one have as a suitable share of something.

examples.text: to allow a servant his liberty; to allow a free passage; to allow one day for rest

glosses: To permit, to give permission to.

examples.text: I will allow my son to be absent.

glosses: To acknowledge, accept the truth of; to concede; to accede to an opinion.

examples.text: to allow a right; to allow a claim; to allow an appeal

glosses: To grant (something) as a deduction or an addition; especially to abate or deduct.

examples.text: to allow a sum for leakage

glosses: To make an allowance, to take into account when making plans.

examples.text: When calculating a budget for a construction project, always allow for contingencies.

glosses: To render physically possible.

examples.text: Truly ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers

glosses: To sanction; to invest; to entrust.
